about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Firm Mexican demand and a lagging harvest (88% done vs a faster average; Iowa 84% vs 95% normally) gave Dec corn a small gain to ~448.75 while the rest of the complex sold off. Inspections slipped on the week, so the export story is strong sales rather than shipments so far.
events: Corn harvest 88% done, behind average; Iowa 84% vs 95% normal (USDA via Successful Farming, Brownfield)
Corn edges higher as soybeans and wheat fall on a strong dollar (AgWeb)
Corn and soybean export inspections slip (MarketWatch)

soybeans.fundamental: Record NOPA crush and faster-than-last-year inspections back demand, but beans eased to ~1229 as the dollar firmed and soyoil fell. The China tariff level is still the swing factor for export demand.
events: NOPA October crush a record (Barchart)
Soybean inspections running ahead of last year (Brownfield)
Trump–Xi summit puts the 10% China tariff in focus (AgroLatam)

meal.fundamental: Meal gained (~332.4 Jan) as the record crush is being driven by oil-share weakness rather than meal demand; still, the crush-margin shift favours meal over oil short-term.
events: Jan meal +4.6 to ~332.4 while soyoil falls (CBOT via TradingView)
Record NOPA crush (Barchart)

oil.fundamental: Soyoil fell ~2.5% with crude down 4%, which cuts biofuel margins. Chevron restarting an Iowa biodiesel plant on demand is a small offset.
events: Jan soyoil -1.57 to ~62.48, tracking crude lower (CBOT via TradingView)
Chevron to restart an Iowa biodiesel plant (Farm Progress)
IEA sees a global oil surplus in Q4 (ADMIS)

wheat.fundamental: Optimism that trilateral talks could free up Black Sea shipping took Dec Chicago down ~6 to 587, and winter wheat condition keeps improving. Both point to easier supply.
events: Wheat falls on hopes talks will free up Black Sea trade (Bloomberg)
US winter wheat conditions improve again (USDA via Farm Progress)
Bulgaria rescues crew from a capsized wheat ship in the Black Sea (Reuters)

kc.fundamental: HRW followed Chicago down (Dec ~619, -9.75): better winter wheat ratings in the Plains and the Black Sea peace trade both weigh.
events: Dec KC wheat -9.75 to ~619 (CBOT via TradingView)
Winter wheat conditions continue to improve (Farm Progress)

cotton.fundamental: Dec settled 76.95 on its low, through 77.05 support, on the dollar and broad commodity selling rather than new crop news. Old-crop Dec/Mar is where the risk is: funds remain long and certified stocks near delivery would not be benign for longs.
events: Dec cotton 76.95 (-1.83), Mar 80.88 (ICE via TradingView)
Broad risk-off: equities, metals and energy lower, dollar firm (Yahoo Finance)

hogs.fundamental: Hogs slipped (Feb ~60.7) despite better pork margins; winter PRRS pressure and large open interest keep the trade nervous near contract lows.
events: Lean hogs edge up from contract lows as pork margins improve, then fade Monday (The Pig Site, Barchart)
PRRS surge flagged for winter swine health (Pork Business)
Europe's top pork producer ousts CEO amid slump (Bloomberg)

cattle.fundamental: The screwworm outbreak has widened, with infestations now reported past 100 across Texas, New Mexico and Arizona; that raises the odds of movement restrictions and a longer wait for Mexican feeder imports. Monday's cash was disappointing and futures corrected (Feb ~224.25), while Tyson flags its beef business still under pressure from tight supplies.
events: New World screwworm spreading quickly across southwestern states (Successful Farming, Drovers)
Cattle correct on disappointing fed cash (AgWeb)
Tyson guides lower sales as beef unit stays under pressure (WSJ, Reuters)

feeders.fundamental: Screwworm spread across the Southwest is the key new risk: it delays any reopening to Mexican feeders and could restrict movements within affected states. Futures eased (Jan ~333.1) with live cattle on a weak cash trade.
events: Screwworm infestations top 100 across TX, NM and AZ (Global Agriculture, Drovers)
Jan feeders -2.25 to ~333.1 (CME via TradingView)

class3.fundamental: HPAI is back in Oklahoma dairy herds, a reminder that infections can cut local milk output, but more cheese and whey supply keeps pressure on Class III.
events: HPAI returns to Oklahoma dairy herds after two years (Dairy Herd)
More cheese and whey output weighs on milk prices (Farm Progress)
CME spot mixed, butter +2 cents (Brownfield)

class4.fundamental: Butter firmed on the spot market while NDM fell; HPAI in new herds is a small supply risk.
events: Butter +2 cents on CME spot Monday (Brownfield)
HPAI returns to Oklahoma dairy herds (Dairy Herd)

palm.fundamental: Palm drifted lower (~4,516 front) with soyoil and crude; nothing new on supply beyond the heavy stocks already in the data.
events: Palm front month -31 to ~4,516 (Bursa via TradingView)
Soyoil and crude both sharply lower Monday (CBOT, NYMEX)

natgas.fundamental: Mild weather is outweighing record US LNG feedgas flows; Dec near 3.12 with the storage surplus over the 5-year average widening.
events: Weak weather outweighs record LNG as futures slip (Natural Gas Intelligence)
US LNG flows hit a record high (OilPrice.com, Bloomberg)
European gas slumps on milder weather (OilPrice.com)

crude.fundamental: WTI fell about 4% to ~85 as the IEA's Q4 surplus view and Iran/Ukraine peace hopes outweighed the Houthi threat to Saudi exports. It sits just under 85.63 resistance, with 77 the next support well below.
events: Oil falls on expected supply surplus (Reuters)
IEA expects a global surplus in Q4 (ADMIS)
Houthi advance puts Saudi crude exports at risk (OilPrice.com)

ulsd.fundamental: Diesel fell nearly 5% to ~4.06, below the 100-day fund trigger, as retail diesel dropped under $6 on easing tensions and softer demand. Distillate stocks are still below average, so this is a price-led unwind rather than a supply glut.
events: US retail diesel below $6/gal at a two-month low (Reuters, Bloomberg)
ULSD Dec ~4.06, below the 100-day average (NYMEX)

rbob.fundamental: Gasoline slid ~3.7% with crude; nothing new on supply.
events: RBOB Jan ~2.49 (-3.7%) with crude (NYMEX)
Crude lower on surplus outlook (Reuters)
